title: Seeds and Sprouts
objectives: I can tell what a seed, soil, and a plant are.
I can tell how a seed grows and sprouts.
I can draw and say how a plant gets bigger.
rationale: This first science unit follows one familiar sequence, from seed to sprout to plant, so the five words connect into a single picture that children can watch in a real cup on a window sill. Seed and soil are Tier 3 words that name the things in the picture; plant, grow, and sprout name what happens. Plant is also a verb in everyday talk, but only the noun is taught here. The unit revisits tall, stretch, and count, since children measure and describe how a plant changes.

passage.title: Omar's Bean
paras: Omar puts a bean seed in the soil. He gives it water every day.
Soon a tiny green plant begins to sprout. Omar counts three leaves.
The plant will grow tall and stretch toward the sun. Omar smiles and waits for more leaves.

teacher.overview: Children learn five plant words by planting a bean in a clear cup and watching it, then hear the words in a short story about a boy's bean plant. The work is hands-on and spoken; children draw what they see.

notes.va.seed.n: Use a dry bean and a lima bean soaked overnight. Seed is a tiny beginning, not a baby plant, so show that a seed is dry and still before it starts to grow. Keep to true facts: apples and beans have seeds.
notes.va.soil.n: Tier 3 word. Let children touch soil and compare with sand and with a rock. Soil is not the same as mud; mud is wet soil. Plants also can grow in other things, but this unit says soil.
notes.va.plant.n: Teach the noun, a living green thing that grows. Plant is also a verb, as in plant a seed, and a factory. Say only the noun first, and notice when children use plant as a verb.
notes.va.grow.v: Measure the plant each day and count how much taller it is. Grow means get bigger over time. Children also grow, so link it to them: puppies, babies, and plants all grow.
notes.va.sprout.v: Sprout is the first green shoot. A seed needs water and warmth to sprout. Have children say 'sprouted' when a bean shows a root or shoot, since the word is also used as a noun, which is not taught here.

teacher.model: Think-aloud: 'I put the seed in the soil, the dirt that plants grow in. I give it water. In a few days a tiny green shoot will sprout. Then the plant will grow bigger. Let's count the leaves and say the words.'
discuss: What does a seed need to sprout?
What can you grow from a seed?
misconceptions: A seed is already a small plant.
Soil is the same as mud or sand.
Plants only grow in a garden.
extend: Plant beans in clear cups and draw the plant each day for two weeks.
Measure the plant with cubes and count how many tall it has grown.
teacher.reviewAdvice: Revisit tall, stretch, and count when children measure the plant: 'How tall is it? Count the cubes. Let's stretch like a plant.' Use grow and sprout again in unit 11 when characters change in stories.

wida.oral: Partner A shows a picture card of seed, sprout, or plant. Partner B names the picture and says one thing the seed needs, using the frame.

needsReview: Spanish glosses (semilla, tierra, planta, crecer, brotar) have not been reviewed by a native speaker; tierra also means land and earth and may need a picture note.
Sense boundary: plant is taught only as the noun (a living green thing); the verb (to plant a seed) and the factory sense are left out, though planted may appear in talk.
Sense boundary: sprout is taught as a verb (start to grow with a green shoot); the noun sense (a bean sprout to eat) is left out.
Fact check: seeds need water and warmth to sprout; the unit does not claim sun or soil is needed for sprouting. Bean seeds sprout in a few days to about a week, so no exact time is stated.
The synonym greenery for plant is loose and only meant for teachers; no close one-word synonym exists.
